subject: MerchantX GPU fleet shape questionnaire and commit forecast
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Rajesh Patel <rajesh.patel@merchantx.com>; Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@merchantx.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MerchantX GPU fleet shape questionnaire and commit forecast

Hi Rajesh / Lina —

Thanks for taking the call last week. To speed the Dedicated sizing work and give you a reliable commit forecast for procurement, can you confirm the quick traffic/profile details below? We can slot assumptions on anything you don't have right now, but the more concrete the numbers the tighter our sizing.

Short answers preferred (a line each) —
- Expected 95th percentile concurrent sessions at peak (weekday peak) and typical sustained concurrency (e.g., 5k p95, 1.2k sustained)
- Average and p95 prompt length (tokens) and average + p95 model response length (tokens)
- Percent of requests that are streaming vs non-streaming (approx)
- Average session duration (seconds) and whether KV-cache reuse is expected across turns (yes/no + reuse % estimate)
- Ratio of interactive traffic vs asynchronous batch inference (percent)
- Expected daily peak window(s) (local timezone) and whether weekend profile differs materially
- Any hard latency SLOs (p95 token latency target / end-to-end response p95)
- Are you planning function/tool calling or heavy tool I/O per request?
- Anticipated go-live commit (month) and preferred procurement cadence (quarterly/annual)

If you have a short CSV or a sample trace, attach it — that helps a lot. I attached a one-page template for the numbers if you want to drop them in.

Goal: produce a preliminary GPU SKU mix and a conservative reserved capacity commit recommendation within 48 hours.

Thanks,
Avery Johnson
Enterprise Solutions (Pre-sales) | Redwood Inference
Schedule: https://cal.redwood.com/avery

[Attachment: merchantx-sizing-template.csv (text/csv)]

From: Rajesh Patel <rajesh.patel@merchantx.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@merchantx.com>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MerchantX GPU fleet shape questionnaire and commit forecast

Avery —

Thanks, quick answers inline below. I've attached a sample traffic export (anonymized) and a session trace screenshot. Happy to jump on a short call if anything needs clarification.

- P95 concurrency / sustained: 4200 p95 at peak, ~900 sustained during business hours (PST).
- Prompt length: avg 120 tokens, p95 420 tokens. Response length: avg 250 tokens, p95 1,200 tokens.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: ~70% streaming (progressive UI), 30% non-streaming batch-like inference.
- Session duration: avg 35s; KV-cache reuse: yes, estimated 60% of sessions will reuse a single KV cache across turns.
- Interactive vs batch: 85% interactive, 15% async/queue.
- Peak windows: 10:00–14:00 PST and 18:00–20:00 PST; weekends ~20% of weekday peak.
- Latency SLOs: p95 end-to-end < 500ms for short queries; for long responses we target p95 token latency < 120ms.
- Tooling: yes, occasional tool calls (~8% of requests), mostly small external lookups.
- Go-live: target 2029-08-01; procurement prefers annual commit but can do quarterly if necessary.

Attachments: merchantx-traffic-sample.csv, merchantx-session-trace.png

—Rajesh
Director of Platform — MerchantX

Rajesh — great, this is very helpful. A couple of clarifying points and our preliminary assumptions below so you know how we'll size: 

Clarifying questions:
- The response p95 of 1,200 tokens — is that often generated in a single turn or split across streaming chunks? (impacts KV / kernel selection)
- For the 8% tool calling: are those calls synchronous blocking calls, or do you stream updates while the tool runs?

Prelim sizing assumptions (we'll run a detailed simulator once we have the CSV):
- Context window assumption: 8k tokens for everyone (covers p95 response+prompt with headroom). If you plan to use >8k, tell us and we'll re-run.
- Target per-token p95 latency target: 120ms for generation-heavy flows; we map that to a mix of A100-80GB and RTX8000 (quantized) for cost/latency tradeoffs.
- KV-cache reuse of 60% reduces per-session peak throughput by ~18% in our model; we'll account for that.
- For 4.2k p95 concurrent with 70% streaming and avg response sizes, conservative reserved capacity recommendation: 28 x A100-80GB equivalent (this is a starting point; final number depends on batching, quantization, and session shapes).

Next steps:
1) We'll run the traffic CSV through our sizing simulator and send a short slide with two commit options (conservative and optimized) by EOD tomorrow.
2) If MerchantX is comfortable, we recommend a 12-month reserved commit with a 3-month ramp (helps secure capacity and lower unit cost).
3) Can procurement share preferred billing/legal milestones so we can attach a draft SOW to the recommendation?

We'll keep latency-budget, token-cost, and fallback model variants visible in the slide.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

[Attachment referenced: internal-sizing-assumption.md — internal use]

Marissa —

Thanks for the initial assumptions, that matches our expectations. Quick notes:
- The 1,200 p95 responses are typically produced in a single generation pass but streamed to the UI in chunks (so streaming assumptions stand).
- Tool calls are synchronous; UI waits for the tool response before finishing a turn.
- Procurement attached our preferred timeline and milestones (see attached PDF). We're leaning toward an annual commit but want the 3-month ramp you suggested.

Can you include an option in the slide deck that assumes 12k context for a small subset (10% of sessions) — we may pilot a long-doc summarization feature. If that materially changes commit, flag it so procurement sees the delta.

If possible, aim to have the preliminary two-option slide by EOD tomorrow; procurement will review it on Friday.

—Rajesh
Director of Platform — MerchantX
